items.stem: Which component was added to the working memory model by Baddeley in 2000?
items.answer: The episodic buffer

items.stem: Explain how the serial position effect supports the multi-store model.
items.answer: Primacy reflects early items rehearsed into LTM and recency reflects items still in STM; Glanzer and Cunitz (1966) found a delay removed only recency, suggesting two separate stores.

items.stem: Tomás writes: "Working memory is the same as long-term memory." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Working memory is a temporary, limited-capacity system for holding and manipulating information; LTM is a durable store.
items.markingKey: Working memory is a temporary, limited-capacity system for holding and manipulating information; LTM is a durable store. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in Landry and Bartling (2011), and explain how the dependent variable was operationalised.

items.stem: With reference to Glanzer and Cunitz (1966), explain how research has investigated separate short-term and long-term stores in the multi-store model.
items.answer: Glanzer and Cunitz (1966). Aim: to investigate whether a delay before recall affects primacy and recency effects. Method: US army enlisted men heard lists of 15 words and recalled them either immediately or after a 10- or 30-second delay filled with counting. Findings: immediate recall showed both primacy and recency; with a 30-second delay the recency effect disappeared while primacy remained Link: separate short-term and long-term stores in the multi-store model.
items.markingKey: Up to 2 marks for accurate description of the study (aim, method, findings: immediate recall showed both primacy and recency; with a 30-second delay the recency effect disappeared while primacy remained); up to 2 marks for explicitly linking the findings to separate short-term and long-term stores in the multi-store model. A study that is described but not linked cannot score more than half marks.

items.stem: Describe the study by Peterson and Peterson (1959) and explain what it shows about the brief duration of short-term memory without rehearsal.
items.answer: Peterson and Peterson (1959). Aim: to investigate how long information remains in short-term memory without rehearsal. Method: 24 students heard consonant trigrams (e.g. "KTH") and counted backwards in threes from a given number for 3-18 seconds before recall. Findings: recall fell sharply: about 80% after 3 seconds and about 10% after 18 seconds Link: the brief duration of short-term memory without rehearsal.
items.markingKey: Up to 3 marks for accurate description of the study (aim, method, findings: recall fell sharply: about 80% after 3 seconds and about 10% after 18 seconds); up to 3 marks for explicitly linking the findings to the brief duration of short-term memory without rehearsal. A study that is described but not linked cannot score more than half marks.

items.stem: Explain why the working memory model replaced the idea of a single short-term store.
items.answer: Dual-task studies show people can do a verbal and a visual task at the same time with little interference but not two verbal tasks, suggesting separate subsystems (phonological loop and visuospatial sketchpad) rather than one unitary store.

items.stem: Explain the difference between primacy and recency.
items.answer: Primacy is better recall of the first items in a list (thought to be due to rehearsal into LTM); recency is better recall of the last items (still held in STM).

items.stem: A student revises vocabulary by repeating words aloud while also listening to a podcast. Using the working memory model, explain why this may be ineffective.
items.answer: Both repeating words and listening to speech use the phonological loop, so the two tasks compete for the same limited-capacity subsystem and interfere, reducing encoding.
items.markingKey: Both repeating words and listening to speech use the phonological loop, so the two tasks compete for the same limited-capacity subsystem and interfere, reducing encoding.

items.stem: Outline one way in which remembering a phone number shows the multi-store model.

items.stem: State the aim of the study by Bransford and Johnson (1972) on context and comprehension of a passage.
items.answer: Aim: to investigate whether activating a schema before reading improves comprehension and recall.
